tagline: Twelve miles of switchbacks, then the roof of the plateau.
intro: Out of Red Lodge, an old coal town at the foot of the Beartooth Mountains, US 212 climbs the switchbacks above Rock Creek, from about 5,200 feet to nearly 11,000 in twelve miles, and crosses into Wyoming. Over Beartooth Pass at 10,947 feet it levels out on a wide plateau among lakes, then comes down past the Chief Joseph junction and back into Montana at Cooke City, by Yellowstone's northeast entrance.
General Sheridan crossed here in 1872 with 120 men on an old hunter's say-so, and the road that opened in 1936 mostly follows him. Snow keeps it shut most of the year.

moments.title: Vista Point
moments.text: A stop on the climb out of Red Lodge, looking down the main canyon of Rock Creek.

moments.title: Beartooth Basin Ski Area
moments.text: The only ski area in North America open only in summer, since the highway it depends on is closed all winter. Two platter lifts, and no lodge.

moments.title: Cooke City
moments.text: Named for Jay Cooke, who financed the Northern Pacific, the town sits at about 7,600 feet in the valley of Soda Butte Creek, northeast of the park.

practical: The highway usually opens Memorial Day weekend and closes in mid-October, weather permitting. Snow lingers at the top until early to mid-July, and Montana closes the road every winter.
